title: Atuin Threads lets you resume an agent session on another machine
friendlyTitle: Atuin Threads lets you pick up an agent session on another computer
summary: Atuin 18.24 adds Threads, a searchable history of agent sessions that can sync across machines. You can resume a session, or fork it into a different harness. The first supported agents are Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Omp, and OpenCode. Capture is opt-in. Synced history is end-to-end encrypted. You can use Atuin's server, run your own, or keep it local. An MCP server, installed with atuin mcp install, lets a later agent search prior sessions.
friendlySummary: Atuin 18.24 adds Threads, a searchable history of agent sessions that can sync across computers. You can resume a session, or move it into a different agent. The first supported agents are Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Omp, and OpenCode. Recording is off until you turn it on. Synced history is end-to-end encrypted, so Atuin cannot read it. You can use Atuin's server, run your own, or keep everything local. A later agent can search old sessions through an MCP server, installed with atuin mcp install.
whyItMatters: Shell history already follows you. Agent transcripts usually do not. If you start a task on a server and finish it on a laptop, Threads is a way to carry the prompt, the commands, and the dead ends without pasting them. Team sharing is not shipped. The post is the product note, not an independent review.
